t.1.126.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When way had been made for him by the men, their eyes wide open with wonder, Karṇa, conqueror of enemy cities, entered the vast arena.
t.1.126.2: Wearing the armor he was born with, his face lit up by his earrings, bearing his bow and with his sword girded on, he was like a mountain walking on foot.
t.1.126.3: Karṇa, the slayer of hosts of foes, of far-spread fame and wide eyes, the child Pṛthā bore while still a maiden, a portion of the sharp-rayed Sun, the maker of light.
t.1.126.5: Tall, shining like a golden palm tree, with a lion's build, young, glorious, and possessed of countless virtues, he was the very son born of Bhāskara, the Sun.
t.1.126.4: He was equal in might and prowess to lions, bulls, and lordly elephants, and in his qualities of brilliance, beauty, and splendor he resembled the sun, the moon, and fire.
t.1.126.6: Having surveyed the arena on every side, the mighty-armed one made a salutation to Droṇa and Kṛpa, as though without much respect.
t.1.126.7: That whole assembled crowd became motionless, with eyes fixed and unblinking; stirred with agitation, wondering "Who is this?", they were overcome with curiosity.
t.1.126.8: Then he, the son of Savitṛ, best of speakers, spoke in a voice deep as a thundercloud, a brother addressing his unrecognized brother, the son of Pākaśāsana.
t.1.126.10: Then, O best of speakers, before his words were even finished, the people everywhere quickly rose up, as if hurled upward by a machine.
t.1.126.9: Pārtha, whatever feat you have performed, I shall perform one surpassing it while these men look on; do not be so amazed at yourself.
t.1.126.11: Then, O tiger among men, joy touched Duryodhana, and in an instant shame and anger entered Bībhatsu.
t.1.126.12: Then, permitted by Droṇa, the mighty Karṇa, ever fond of battle, did all that Pārtha had done there.
t.1.126.13: Then Duryodhana there, together with his brothers, O Bhārata, joyfully embraced Karṇa and thereupon spoke these words.
t.1.126.14: Welcome to you, O mighty-armed one; by good fortune you have come, O giver of honor. Let both me and the kingdom of the Kurus be enjoyed by you as you wish.
t.1.126.16: Enjoy pleasures together with me, and be one who does what is dear to your kinsmen; place your foot upon the head of all your foes, O tamer of enemies!
t.1.126.15: I have no need of anything else; I choose friendship with you, and I wish to fight a single combat with Pārtha, O Bhārata.
t.1.126.17: Then Pārtha, deeming himself as if insulted, addressed Karṇa, who stood like a mountain in the midst of the throng of brothers.
t.1.126.18: The worlds that await those who come uninvited and those who speak uninvited, to those worlds, Karṇa, you shall go, slain by me.
t.1.126.19: This arena is common to all; what claim have you here, Phalguna? Kṣatriyas are ranked by valour, and dharma follows strength.
t.1.126.21: Then, permitted by Droṇa, Pārtha, conqueror of enemy cities, hastily embraced by his brothers, went up to him for battle.
t.1.126.20: What use are insults, which are only the comfort of the weak? Speak with arrows, Bhārata, until today, in the presence of your teacher, I take off your head with my arrows!
t.1.126.22: Then Karṇa, eager for battle, embraced by Duryodhana together with his brothers, stood there, grasping his bow with its arrow.
t.1.126.23: Then the sky was covered with clouds accompanied by lightning and thunder, preceded by rainbows, and laughing with rows of cranes.
t.1.126.25: Then the Pāṇḍava was seen enveloped in the shadow of the clouds, while Karṇa too was seen encompassed by the blaze of the sun.
t.1.126.24: Then the Sun, too, seeing Harihaya watching the arena, out of affection drove away the clouds that had gathered near.
t.1.126.26: The Dhārtarāṣṭras took their stand in that place where Karṇa was; Bhāradvāja, Kṛpa and Bhīṣma went over to the side where Pārtha was.
t.1.126.27: The arena was split in two, and a division arose among the women as well; the daughter of Kuntibhoja, understanding what it meant, fell into a swoon.
t.1.126.28: Seeing Kuntī thus overcome by a swoon, Vidura, who knew all the laws of dharma, sprinkled her with water mixed with sandalwood and revived her.
t.1.126.30: To those two, who stood with their great bows raised, spoke Kṛpa Śāradvata, skilled in the conventions of single combat and knowing all the laws of dharma.
t.1.126.29: Then, when her breath had returned, she saw both her sons clad in armor, and, deeply distressed, she could not decide on anything at all.
t.1.126.31: This younger son of Pṛthā, the delight of Pāṇḍu, a Kaurava, will engage in single combat with you.
t.1.126.32: You too, O mighty-armed one, should likewise declare your mother, your father, and the lineage of the kings whose line you carry forward. Then, having learned of you, Pārtha will decide whether or not he will fight against you.
t.1.126.33: When Karṇa was addressed thus, his face, bowed down with shame, looked like a lotus drenched by rainwater and drooping.
t.1.126.35: If this Phalguna does not wish to fight in battle with one who is not a king, then I hereby consecrate this man as king over the land of Aṅga.
t.1.126.34: O teacher, in the settled judgment of the treatises, the origin of kings is threefold: one born of a royal family, a hero, and one who leads an army.
t.1.126.36: Then, at that very moment, the great chariot-warrior Karṇa, seated on a golden seat, was consecrated to the kingship of Aṅga by men versed in mantras, with golden jars filled with parched grain and flowers; and that mighty one became endowed with royal splendor.
t.1.126.37: Then King Vṛṣa, furnished with a fine parasol and a yak-tail fan, spoke amid the cries of victory to that king, the Kaurava.
t.1.126.39: Thus addressed, Karṇa then replied, "So be it." And the two, embracing each other out of joy, attained the highest delight.
t.1.126.38: "What shall I give you that is equal to this gift of a kingdom? Speak, tiger among kings, for I will do just that, O king." Suyodhana said to him, "I desire boundless friendship."
